**Supplementary Table S14. Drop-one influence of individual centuries.** For each climatic term of the evaluated models: *p*-value with all data, largest *p*-value when one century is removed, the century whose removal gives that value, and the percentage of drop-one fits in which the term remains significant.

```{r drop one infl}
dropone <- purrr::pmap_dfr(filter(val_models, Type != "Reference"), function(Panel, Type, Model) {
  d  <- as.data.frame(val_data[[Panel]]) %>% arrange(age)
  f  <- val_formula(Type, Model, d); cb <- Type == "Combined"
  p_full <- term_pvalues(fit_val(f, d, cb))
  p_full <- p_full[names(p_full) != "s(age)"]
  p_drop <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i) {
    m <- fit_val(f, d[-i, ], cb)
    if (is.null(m)) return(setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(p_full)), names(p_full)))
    term_pvalues(m)[names(p_full)]
  })
  p_drop <- matrix(p_drop, nrow = length(p_full), dimnames = list(names(p_full), NULL))
  tibble::tibble(Panel = Panel, Type = Type, Model = Model, Term = names(p_full),
                 p_all = p_full,
                 p_max = apply(p_drop, 1, max, na.rm = TRUE),
                 century_max = d$age[apply(p_drop, 1, which.max)],
                 pct_signif = 100 * rowMeans(p_drop < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE))
})

tab_S14 <- dropone %>%
  mutate(Panel = factor(Panel, levels = site_order),
         Type  = factor(Type, levels = c("Marginal", "Combined")),
         `p (all data)` = fmt_p2(p_all),
         `Largest p (drop-one)` = fmt_p2(p_max),
         `Century removed (ka)` = sprintf("%.1f", century_max),
         `Drop-one fits with p < 0.05 (%)` = sprintf("%.0f", pct_signif)) %>%
  arrange(Panel, Type) %>%
  select(Panel, Type, Model, Term, `p (all data)`, `Largest p (drop-one)`,
         `Century removed (ka)`, `Drop-one fits with p < 0.05 (%)`) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Panel") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Drop-one influence of individual centuries on the climatic terms")
tab_S14
gt::gtsave(tab_S14, "Supplementary_Table_S14.docx")
```

- **Cross-validation.** Only the marginal thermal-regime model of Punta Maroma predicts better than the reference model in both versions (ΔELPD = 31.1 ± 23.0 in LOO, 26.3 ± 19.6 in h-block; 71 % of the centuries predicted better), and its summed differences are of the same order as their standard errors. The marginal hurricane-regime model of the regional composite is better in LOO (13.5 ± 12.8) but not in h-block (−9.6 ± 4.3). All selected combined models have negative summed differences in LOO and h-block (e.g. Punta Maroma: −41.9 ± 39.5 and −10.6 ± 44.8; regional composite: −3.0 ± 9.0 and −40.3 ± 20.5), although they predict 58–65 % of the left-out centuries better than the reference model; the losses are concentrated in a few centuries (worst: 5.0 ka in Punta Maroma, 5.2 ka in Belize, 0.2 ka in the regional composite). In Florida and Saint Croix no climate model is better than the reference model. With 19–57 centuries per panel, cross-validation does not discriminate firmly among models; the fitted models describe the sampled record and have limited predictive transferability beyond its climatic range.
- **Circular-shift test.** The marginal models of Punta Maroma (thermal regime, *p* = 0.04) and of the regional composite (hurricane regime, *p* = 0.02, the smallest attainable) exceed nearly all or all shifted alignments, whereas the selected combined models of both panels do not reach α = 0.05 (*p* = 0.06 and 0.08). In Belize *p* = 0.12 (marginal) and 0.26 (combined) (not all 49 shifted fits converge for this model, so its *p*-value is not a multiple of 1/50), in Florida 0.08 and 0.64, and in Saint Croix 0.16 and 0.26: in these panels the observed alignment is not distinguishable from a shifted one at α = 0.05.
- **Drop-one influence.** In Punta Maroma the thermal regime remains significant in 97 % of the drop-one fits of both models; its largest *p* (0.66 marginal, 0.44 combined) occurs on removing 0.1 ka. In the regional composite the hurricane regime remains significant in 98 % of the fits of both models (largest *p* = 0.065 and 0.083, again on removing 0.1 ka). In Florida s(Hur100_fqcy) remains significant in every drop-one fit of the combined model (largest *p* = 0.009, on removing 5.9 ka) and in 25 % of the marginal fits. In Belize s(dT_raw) and the hurricane regime remain significant in 95 % and 90 % of the combined fits, s(GMHT_CPS0_30N) in 57 % and the thermal regime in 38 %; the marginal s(GMHT_CPS0_30N) remains significant in 96 % (largest *p* = 0.096, on removing 0.2 ka). The century with most influence on the selected regime terms of Punta Maroma and the regional composite is the youngest (0–0.1 ka), which is examined further in Section 4.5.2.
- **Former cross-validation.** Because the Regional panel contains the site records, every observation entered the training data twice, and the score was computed against the mean of 4–6 test values per panel and fold. When those values are nearly identical, as is common with 2–6 distinct response values per site, the denominator approaches zero and the score becomes very negative or undefined (median of fold means −13.6 in Punta Maroma; undefined folds in 11 and 20 of the 20 fold assignments in Belize and Saint Croix). Its results therefore do not measure the predictive performance of the site models, and the analysis is replaced by the cross-validation above.

```{r}
## ---- (4) former five-fold cross-validation (withdrawn) -------------------------
## One model fitted to all panels pooled (each record enters twice through the Regional
## panel), stratified 5-fold split, score = 1 - SSE/SST with SST around the TEST-fold mean.
old_cv <- function(seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  dd <- as.data.frame(merged_df_g)
  fo <- integer(nrow(dd))
  for (p in unique(dd$panel)) {
    i <- which(dd$panel == p); fo[i] <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = length(i)))
  }
  purrr::map_dfr(1:5, function(k) {
    m  <- bam(counts_norm_sv ~ s(age) + s(Hur100_av), data = dd[fo != k, ],
              family = betar(link = "logit"), method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE)
    te <- dd[fo == k, ] %>% mutate(pred = predict(m, ., type = "response"))
    te %>% group_by(panel) %>%
      summarise(score = 1 - sum((counts_norm_sv - pred)^2) /
                  sum((counts_norm_sv - mean(counts_norm_sv))^2),
                n_test = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
      mutate(seed = seed, fold = k)
  })
}
old_cv_res <- purrr::map_dfr(1:20, old_cv)

old_cv_res %>%
  group_by(panel, seed) %>%
  summarise(mean_score = mean(score), n_test = mean(n_test), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Panel = panel) %>%
  summarise(`Test points per fold` = round(mean(n_test), 1),
            `Median of fold means` = signif(median(mean_score[is.finite(mean_score)]), 3),
            `Range of fold means`  = paste(signif(range(mean_score[is.finite(mean_score)]), 3),
                                           collapse = " to "),
            `Assignments with an undefined fold` = sum(!is.finite(mean_score)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Panel = factor(Panel, levels = site_order)) %>% arrange(Panel) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Former five-fold cross-validation, re-run over 20 random fold assignments")
```

### 4.7 Time reference, bin phase, regime models and the Little Ice Age contrast

These analyses were added in the third round of revision, after the hurricane metrics were recounted in BP bins (Section 1.2). They test four questions that the analyses of Sections 4.5 and 4.6 leave open: whether the results depend on (i) how the youngest bin is closed and on the time reference of the bins, (ii) where the century boundaries fall (bin phase), (iii) age and sampling uncertainty in the models that are now selected, which contain categorical regimes (M6, M7), and (iv) the modern century, for the Little Ice Age contrast of Punta Maroma. All four were specified before they were run. Each chunk reads the stored results; `rerun_round3 <- TRUE` recomputes them (about 3 h). The functions are in `sensitivity_round3/round3_functions.R`.

```{r round3-setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
rerun_round3 <- FALSE
r3 <- function(...) here("sensitivity_round3", ...)
source(r3("round3_functions.R"))
```

#### 4.7.1 Youngest bin and time reference

The main analysis closes the youngest bin at the youngest dated colony (1956 CE), as for the coral ages. Two alternatives were run through the complete pipeline: the youngest bin extended to 2022 CE as a rate per century (climate table `df_GAM130326_regimes_v4c.xlsx`), and every series expressed in years before 2021 CE, the reference of the U-Th ages of Punta Maroma (coral ages + 0.071 ka; TC events re-counted from the individual event layers of Schmitt et al. 2025, table S4a; temperature and regimes re-assigned by overlap; climate table `sensitivity_round3/df_GAM130326_regimes_2021frame.xlsx`). The table below reports the selected combined model of each run and the AIC advantage over `s(age)` with and without the youngest bin.

```{r round3-frames}
frames_t2 <- read.csv(r3("frames_table2.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
frames_yb <- read.csv(r3("frames_youngest_bin.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
frames_t2 %>% select(Frame, Panel, Selected, Weight, DevExpl, Significant) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Frame") %>% tab_header(title = "Selected combined model under three youngest-bin and time-reference choices")
frames_yb %>% gt(groupname_col = "Frame") %>%
  cols_label(`dAIC_vs_s(age)_all_bins` = "ΔAIC vs s(age), all bins",
             `dAIC_vs_s(age)_without_youngest` = "ΔAIC vs s(age), without youngest bin") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Dependence on the youngest bin")
```

Extending the youngest bin to 2022 CE keeps the main terms of Punta Maroma (thermal regime), the regional composite (hurricane regime) and Belize (temperature and δT, although the regimes drop out of the Belize model), and changes the results of Florida and Saint Croix. Expressing every series in years before 2021 CE changes the picture: s(Hur100_fqcy) becomes significant in every panel, together with the thermal regime, and the support no longer depends on the youngest bin (Punta Maroma 24.5 → 45.0 AIC units without it). Out-of-sample prediction does not improve, however: the combined models of Punta Maroma and the regional composite predict left-out centuries worse than `s(age)` (ΔELPD −77.8 and −12.3). Corals and storms are aligned identically in the two frames; only the century boundaries move, by 71 years. A result that changes with that shift depends on the bin phase, which is tested directly in Section 4.7.2.

#### 4.7.2 Bin phase

The bin origin is shifted by 0, 10, …, 90 years. Coral ages and TC event layers are re-binned exactly; the temperature anomaly is interpolated at the bin centres, and each regime is taken from the BP bin that holds the bin centre. With no shift the ensemble reproduces the selected models of Table 2 in four panels; in Florida it selects M4_fqcy instead of M6_fqcy (Akaike weights 0.20 and 0.22 in Table 2), because counts from individual layers differ by one event from the window counts in two bins.

```{r round3-phase}
if (rerun_round3) {
  phase_ens <- run_phase_ensemble();         write.csv(phase_ens, r3("phase_ensemble.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  phase_cf  <- run_phase_regime_contrasts(); write.csv(phase_cf,  r3("phase_regime_coefs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}
phase_ens <- read.csv(r3("phase_ensemble.csv"))
phase_cf  <- read.csv(r3("phase_regime_coefs.csv"))
phase_ens %>% group_by(Panel = factor(panel, panel_names)) %>%
  summarise(`s(Hur100) p<0.05, marginal (of 10)` = sum(pmin(p_hf_marg, p_hav_marg, na.rm = TRUE) < 0.05),
            `s(Hur100) p<0.05, selected combined` = sum(p_hur_best < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Hurricane regime p<0.05, selected combined` = sum(p_hurreg_best < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Thermal regime p<0.05, selected combined` = sum(p_therm_best < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
            `dAIC selected vs s(age), range` = sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", min(dAIC_comb_vs_M1), max(dAIC_comb_vs_M1)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  gt() %>% tab_header(title = "Phase ensemble: number of the 10 bin phases in which each term is significant")
phase_cf %>% mutate(cell = sprintf("%.2f%s", est, ifelse(p < 0.05, "*", ""))) %>%
  select(panel, level, o, cell) %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = o, values_from = cell) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "panel") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Hurricane-regime contrasts (s(age) + regime; reference 'moderate') by bin shift (yr)",
             subtitle = "* p < 0.05")
```

The continuous TC metrics are significant in few phases: in the marginal models in 3 of 10 phases at Punta Maroma, 2 in the regional composite, 0 at Belize and 3 in Florida, and in the selected combined model in 1–3 phases (7 in Saint Croix, a panel that is not interpreted). The categorical regimes, by contrast, are significant in the selected combined model in most phases: the hurricane regime in 9 phases at Punta Maroma and 7 in the regional composite and at Belize, the thermal regime in 7 at Punta Maroma. The contrasts show which level carries the hurricane regime. Only "high" (0–0.2 ka, the rise after 1800 CE) has a consistent effect: positive in every phase and panel (Punta Maroma +2.5 to +5.2, significant in 10 of 10; regional composite +1.9 to +3.2, 9 of 10; Belize +1.4 to +2.9, 5 of 10). "Enhanced" (0.6–1.4 ka) and "calm" (0.2–0.6 ka) have no consistent effect. The association with the hurricane regime therefore rests on the two most recent centuries. These are "high" in the regime classification of Schmitt et al. (2025), which refers to the rise after 1800 CE including the 20th and 21st centuries; in the counts that fall within our bins, which end at the youngest dated colony (1956 CE), they hold 15 and 11 events, close to the late-Holocene median of 11 events per century. The regime contrast therefore identifies the two centuries, not an excess of storms within them.

#### 4.7.3 Age and sampling uncertainty in all combined candidates

Section 4.5.2(e) refits only M1–M4. Here every combined candidate (M1–M7, after `drop_hydro()`) is refitted in each of about 300 replicates per scenario (two halves, replicates 1–150 and 151–300, seeds 20261006 and 20261007), and the term-level *p*-values of the model selected with the audited ages are recorded.

```{r round3-mc-full}
mc_full_files <- here("M3_sensitivity", c("gam_uncertainty_mc_full_v4b_part1.rds", "gam_uncertainty_mc_full_v4b_part2.rds"))
if (rerun_round3) {
  saveRDS(run_mc_full(1:150, 20261006),   mc_full_files[1])
  saveRDS(run_mc_full(151:300, 20261007), mc_full_files[2])
}
mc_full <- bind_rows(lapply(mc_full_files, readRDS))
mc_full_tbl <- mc_full %>%
  group_by(Panel = factor(Panel, panel_names), Scenario = factor(Scenario, c("Age", "Sampling", "Both"))) %>%
  summarise(Replicates = n(), `Selected (audited ages)` = first(sel),
            `Top model (share)` = { tb <- sort(table(best), decreasing = TRUE); sprintf("%s (%.0f %%)", names(tb)[1], 100 * tb[1] / n()) },
            `Selected model best (%)` = round(100 * mean(best == sel)),
            `Selected within 2 AIC (%)` = round(100 * mean(dAIC_sel <= 2, na.rm = TRUE)),
            `Best includes a regime (%)` = round(100 * mean(grepl("M5|M6|M7", best))),
            `dAIC vs s(age) > 2 (%)` = round(100 * mean(dAIC_M1 > 2, na.rm = TRUE)),
            `Thermal p < 0.05 (%)` = round(100 * mean(p_Thermal < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)),
            `Hurricane regime p < 0.05 (%)` = round(100 * mean(p_Hurricane < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)),
            `s(GMHT) p < 0.05 (%)` = round(100 * mean(p_temp < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)),
            `s(dT_raw) p < 0.05 (%)` = round(100 * mean(p_dt < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)),
            `s(Hur100) p < 0.05 (%)` = round(100 * mean(p_hur < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop")
mc_full_tbl %>% gt(groupname_col = "Panel") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Age and sampling uncertainty propagated to all combined candidates (M1-M7)")
```

In Punta Maroma the best model contains a regime in 95–96 % of the replicates, and the thermal regime of the selected model is significant in 88–100 %; s(Hur100_av) is significant in 18–30 %. In the regional composite the hurricane regime is significant in 81–98 % of the replicates and s(Hur100_av) in 19–22 %. At Belize, s(GMHT_CPS0_30N) is significant in 23–36 % of the replicates, s(dT_raw) in 34–42 % and the regimes in 44–94 %. The model selected with the audited ages is itself the best model in only 4–41 % of the replicates, so the identity of the selected model is uncertain, whereas the presence of a regime term in Punta Maroma and the regional composite is not.

#### 4.7.4 The Little Ice Age contrast of Punta Maroma

The thermal-regime contrast of Punta Maroma (LIA −3.50, reference "warmer"; Table 2) compares the LIA bins with the "warmer" bins, and at this site "warmer" consists of the modern century (normalized density 0.98, the maximum) and three mid-Holocene bins. To test whether the LIA differs from the other cool or warm intervals, independently of the modern century, the two youngest bins (0–0.2 ka) are removed and the reference is set to the Caribbean Warm Period–Medieval Warm Anomaly (CWP&MWA) or, where that regime has no bins, to "cooler". Four specifications are fitted in each of the 10 phases: with `s(age)`, with `s(age, k = 4)`, without `s(age)`, and with the regime lagged by one century.

```{r round3-lia}
if (rerun_round3) write.csv(run_lia_tests(), r3("lia_tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
lia <- read.csv(r3("lia_tests.csv"))
raw_reg <- merged_df_g %>% filter(panel %in% c("Punta Maroma", "Belize", "Regional")) %>%
  group_by(Panel = panel, Thermal) %>%
  summarise(Bins = n(), `Mean density` = round(mean(counts_norm_sv), 3), `Median density` = round(median(counts_norm_sv), 3), .groups = "drop")
raw_reg %>% gt(groupname_col = "Panel") %>% tab_header(title = "Normalized density by thermal regime (all bins, audited ages)")
lia %>% filter(level == "LIA") %>%
  group_by(Panel = panel, Specification = spec) %>%
  summarise(`LIA estimate, range` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", min(est), max(est)),
            `Phases with p < 0.05 (of 10)` = sum(p < 0.05), .groups = "drop") %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Panel") %>%
  tab_header(title = "LIA contrast without the two modern centuries (reference CWP&MWA, or 'cooler' where absent)")
```

In the raw data the LIA bins of Punta Maroma have a mean normalized density of 0.154, against 0.127 in the "cooler" bins and 0.405 in the "warmer" bins, which include the modern maximum. Without the two modern centuries the LIA contrast of Punta Maroma ranges from −0.56 to +0.42 across phases and specifications without the lag (−0.35 to +0.28 with `s(age)`; positive in 9 of 10 phases) and from +0.26 to +1.05 with the lag, and it is not significant in any of the 40 fits. At Belize (−0.79 to +1.00) and in the regional composite (−1.09 to +0.04) the LIA contrast with the CWP&MWA is not significant in any phase or specification. The negative LIA coefficient of Table 2 is therefore a contrast between the LIA and the century that follows it: the low density of the LIA precedes the modern maximum. It does not show lower density during the LIA than during earlier cool intervals. At Punta Maroma the CWP&MWA (0.7–1.3 ka) has no dated colonies; it falls within the 0.64–1.38-ka low-density interval (Section 2), and bins without colonies do not enter the models.

#### 4.7.5 Summary

Across the four tests, two results are stable. First, the frequency of dated colonies is highest in the two most recent centuries, which coincide with the "high" hurricane regime of Schmitt et al. (2025) and with the warm modern regime; this association holds across bin phases, time references and age and sampling uncertainty, but it rests on two bins and cannot be separated from recency bias. Second, at Punta Maroma the LIA bins have lower density than the modern century that follows them, but not lower than earlier cool intervals. The continuous TC metrics (Hur100_fqcy, Hur100_av) are not robust to bin phase or to age and sampling uncertainty, and no climatic predictor shows a consistent association before 0.2 ka.
